blocks.text: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming approach in which a program is designed using objects that represent real-world entities.
A class is a blueprint or template used to create objects. It defines the properties and behaviours of an object.
An object is an instance of a class. It represents a real-world entity with its own data and functions.
Modularity means dividing a program into smaller, manageable parts so that each part can be developed and maintained separately.
Reusability means using already written code again in different parts of a program or in other programs.
Encapsulation is the process of keeping data and related methods together inside a class. It helps protect data from unauthorized access.
Inheritance is an OOP concept in which one class can use the properties and methods of another class.
Polymorphism means using the same method or operation in different ways depending on the object. It helps make code flexible and adaptable.
